title: The Battle of Red Cliffs
content_zh:
Cao Cao amassed an army of eight hundred thousand soldiers. He marched south to conquer the lands of the Sun family and the remnants of Liu Bei's forces. The south trembled.
Zhuge Liang, the Sleeping Dragon, proposed an alliance between Liu Bei and Sun Quan. He went alone into Sun Quan's court, debated the surrender faction, and convinced the young lord to fight.
The southern alliance had one advantage: the Yangtze River. Cao Cao's northern soldiers, unused to naval warfare, grew seasick. An advisor suggested chaining the ships together for stability.
On the night of the battle, Zhou Yu's fireships sailed into the chained fleet. The wind — summoned by Zhuge Liang's prayer, legends say — swept flames across the water. Cao Cao's invincible armada burned to ashes.
